story.head: Pastrňák’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings (8-10-3) beat Tampa Bay 2-0 on Saturday, while the Bruins are on a three-game losing streak. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Bruins fourth (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Red Wings seventh (tied for 25th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Bruins’ record (.643) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.577), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.452) says: their chances are worth about .549, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Bruins (lowest) and the Red Wings (4th lowest) both leave the shooting to their forwards. The Bruins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest) and rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). On the other side, the Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), but ice the puck a lot (30th). The Bruins wait for good looks, but the Wings settle for hopeful ones. On top of that, the Red Wings’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

David Pastrňák (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 21 GP) is carrying the Bruins’ offense, with a point in nine straight games against Detroit. For the Red Wings, Lucas Raymond (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight goals in eleven games against Boston since 2023-24. Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 21 GP) is next in line.
Jeremy Swayman (9-5-1 / .905 SV% in 15 GS) is expected to go for Boston. Daniil Tarasov (3-3-2 / .931 SV% in 7 GS) has been outstanding for Detroit and is expected to start.
